thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: TP job group 'tp4-prod' experiencing repeated NCCL communicator resets and leader re-election. Multiple containers reporting 'rendezvous leader mismatch' and subsequent communicator aborts -> Yields partial pipeline stalls and pod restarts. Auto-fallback to single-device shards triggered for some requests. Seen across two clusters: eu-west-1 and us-west-2.

eric_oncall: acknowledged. I'm on it — collecting logs and tagging. Can people drop immediate diagnostic snippets: `kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide` and `kubectl logs <pod> -c runtime --tail=200` for an affected pod?

miguel_sre: grabbing kube and node metrics. Early read: gworker-12 lost kubelet heartbeat for ~18s then came back; leader election for rendezvous moved from gworker-12 -> gworker-8 -> gworker-12 (flip). NCCL timeouts followed. Pulled partial log from runtime:```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] runtime: NCCL_WARN > COMM_ID_MISMATCH: Rendezvous leader changed during `commInit`.
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] runtime: ERR > ncclCommInitRank failed: NET/RET_ERR (unrecoverable)
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] container: exit code 134 (signal 6)
```
This matches a leader flip race where some ranks try to init with old ring id.

anya_runtime: Confirming. We see sequential communicator resets followed by container restarts on 3 of 12 workers in the job. Runtime telemetry: KV cache invalidated on the restarted ranks, causing 8-12 token latency spikes. Fallback path triggered for ~12% of requests to non-sharded variant (logged as shim-fallback). Sending short stats in a sec.

sara_eng: quick mitigation plan: 1) cordon and drain gworker-12 to stop further leader flaps 2) bump rendezvous leader election timeout to 15s temporarily 3) restart runtime-agent on affected nodes to clear stale communicator state 4) if nodes keep flapping, failover traffic to dedicated pool and rollback to single-node pipeline variant for critical customers.

miguel_sre: adding commands I'm running now:```bash
kubectl cordon gworker-12
kubectl drain gworker-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n redwood-serving
# restart runtime agents on node
ssh ops@gworker-12 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime-agent'
```
Watching node events: kubelet reported 'container runtime network not ready' around the time of the first leader flip. Might be intermittent CNI hiccup + a transient GPU driver glitch.

deploy-bot: Observability alert: autopatch job attempted on gworker-12 yesterday 03:40UTC and applied a kernel module update. No automatic reboot recorded. Patch id: kp-2026-0314-7.

eric_oncall: good catch @deploy-bot. That could explain transient compatibility with the current driver. Priorities: 1) stop more pods from restarting, 2) ensure customer-facing fallbacks stay healthy, 3) assemble incident summary for customers.

beth_support: Customer impact check: product reports increased 5xx rate for 'chat' customers in eu-west-1 and degraded throughput for two named customers (AcmeAI and Finch Labs). Can we get a short impact blurb I can send to CS? Also earliest ETA for mitigation?

anya_runtime: Impact numbers: eu-west-1 cluster: ~9% error rate spike at peak, sustained ~3% errors after fallback. us-west-2: transient 4% spike. Currently ~85% of requests unaffected due to fallback; latency p95 increased from 120ms -> 480ms for sharded path. ETA: drain+restart should be done in 10-20m, then monitor for recurrence. If leader flips repeat, we'll move critical customers to dedicated pool (30-45m).

eric_oncall: Draft for CS: "We detected a rendezvous leader election race that caused NCCL communicator mismatches and several container restarts. We've cordoned the unstable node, restarted runtime agents, and enabled a fallback to single-device sharding for affected requests. Expected to fully restore stable sharded serving in ~20-40 minutes if no further leader flips occur. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes." Shareable?

beth_support: Send that now to CS and include: impacted clusters (eu-west-1, us-west-2), affected customers (AcmeAI, Finch Labs), approximate user-facing error/latency figures, and mitigation actions. I'll coordinate customer outbound. :thumbsup:

miguel_sre: rolling restart done for runtime-agent on gworker-12. Observed container restarts stop after agent restart but I still see a single NCCL timeout event ~2m after restart. Monitoring kernel dmesg on node shows repeated PCIe link retrain messages — could be hardware flakiness.

sara_eng: If PCIe link retrains persist, we should mark node as degraded and move workloads off permanently and replace hardware. For immediate mitigation, enlarge rendezvous election window and ensure leader stickiness on current leader for active jobs: setting `RZ_LEADER_STICKINESS=true` in runtime config for this job family. We can hotpatch the runtime config via ConfigMap and roll only the job controller.

eric_oncall: go ahead with hotpatch but limit blast radius to tp4-prod namespace. miguel, please continue drain if link retrain persists. anya, hold customer traffic fallback policy at current thresholds.

deploy-bot: ConfigMap update applied to tp4-prod: `rz-election-timeout=15s`, `rz-leader-stickiness=true`. Deployment rollout started for job-controller.

anya_runtime: Rollout ok on 6/6 controllers. Observability: communicator resets reduced to near-zero after stickiness and agent restart. Fallback rate dropped from 12% -> 1.5% over 8 minutes. p95 latency trending back toward normal.

miguel_sre: Node gworker-12 still shows PCIe retrain count > 5 in last 10m. I've put it in cordoned-degraded state and opened a hardware ticket with datacenter ops ticket #DC-8721. Replacements scheduled in maintenance window tomorrow.

eric_oncall: thanks. Next steps: 1) keep node cordoned, 2) monitor for 2h, 3) update customer communications with resolved/ongoing items, 4) prepare postmortem if hardware confirmed. I'll hand this off to the evening on-call in 35m. Anyone else to add?

beth_support: I'll send an update to AcmeAI/Finch with the mitigation summary and expected hardware replacement ETA. Will request confirmation if they still see issues.

sara_eng: reminder: open incident ticket (inc-3890123456) and capture timeline + config change (rz-election-timeout + leader stickiness). Add hypothesis: kernel module update + PCIe retrain -> transient driver-level desync -> leader flip.

eric_oncall: creating incident page and assigning to eng-runtime + sre. Handoff note: watch for secondary flips during next 1 hour of peak traffic. If recurrence -> full job evacuation to dedicated pool.

incidents-bot: Incident severity updated -> SEV2 (reduced after mitigation). Handoff to evening oncall @eric_oncall -> @miguel_sre (oncoming). :white_check_mark:

miguel_sre: taking over monitoring. I'll post if any new anomalies.

eric_oncall: thanks team, nice quick remediation. Closing the pager for now; will keep the incident open for postmortem. :coffee:
